title: Retire the Gemini CLI fallback for DeepSeek escalation
body:
Part of #1406 (3 of 4). Stacked on #1413.

- **Gemini removed from self-work.** `gemini-fallback.js`, its takeover path, `benchGemini`, its settings in `.env.sample` and its tests are gone. The `.env.sample` section now describes DeepSeek escalation; its key lives in Settings, not `.env`.
- **Status line.** Self-work's `status()` now reports `escalation: { enabled, text }`, for example "DeepSeek escalation: off -- there's no DeepSeek key in Settings.". The launcher's self-work window shows that line where the Gemini one was.
- **Bench.** `--gemini` becomes `--remote <model> [--thinking on|off]` for #1411. It runs her loop on that DeepSeek model, with her local reviewer on the bench's own llama-server and the key from Settings. Each run's tokens and dollars go in the report (`spend`) and in API spending (use: bench). The bench's token counter now counts remote replies too.
- **Training-traces doc** and the telemetry route treat DeepSeek as a remote model.

Tests: `self-work` 54, `self-work-escalation` 7, `self-work-bench` 17 (Gemini's case replaced by a `--remote` one: no key means no run; otherwise it names the model, thinking setting and reviewer) and `self-work-traces` 5 all pass locally. The launcher's self-work test now reads the escalation line.
interface: The merged change for PR #1414 is covered by test/self-work-bench.test.js, test/self-work-gemini.test.js.
why: Additional real merged-fix benchmark case selected to broaden the agentic coding evaluation.
